event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: CSGP’s 2021 Form 10-K provides extensive, contemporaneous discussion of the COVID-19 pandemic.  The filing, made less than a year after the WHO declaration, treats the pandemic as both an already-realised shock (e.g., higher cancellations, lower bookings, remote-work costs) and a continuing source of uncertainty that could become materially adverse.  Language is generally specific—detailing concrete operational effects such as customer payment failures, workforce relocation costs and productivity impacts—yet most impacts are unquantified and framed as potential or directional rather than numerically measured.  The company acknowledges certain offsets (cost savings, restored sales momentum, no 2020 financial-statement hit), which temper but do not eliminate risk.  Under the Time Decay Principle, the pandemic is a recent (0-3 years) event, so high scores are permissible; however, the mix of realised but modestly sized impacts, forward-looking cautions and explicit mitigations justifies mid-to-high—but not maximum—severity ratings across evidence snippets.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business and results of operations have been and will be, and our financial condition may be, impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and such impact could be materially adverse and continue for an unknown period of time.

components.reason: States impacts have already occurred ('have been') – direct realised effect.
Flags future, indefinite, materially adverse impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct past impact plus projection of unknown-duration material harm warrants a high (but not maximum) recent-event score.

evidence_list.snippet: The global spread of COVID-19 has created significant economic volatility, uncertainty and disruption around the world.

components.reason: Describes broad macroeconomic disruption affecting company context.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures external volatility but does not tie explicitly to quantified corporate outcomes, yielding a modest risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which COVID-19 will further impact our business, operations and financial results, including the duration and magnitude of such impact, is uncertain and will depend on numerous rapidly evolving factors that we cannot accurately predict including, among others:

components.reason: Highlights uncertainty and lack of predictability regarding future impacts.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertainty itself is a risk aggravator, but absence of specifics keeps the score moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of COVID-19 and its impact on global economic conditions, including the real estate industry, towards the end of the first quarter and in the first two months of the second quarter of 2020, we saw an increase in customer requests for cancellations or suspensions, a reduction in new customer sales, failures to pay and delays in payments of amounts owed to us.

components.reason: Reports concrete, realised commercial impacts (cancellations, reduced sales, payment failures).
Provides timing context, confirming recency and direct linkage.
Multiple impact vectors (sales, cash collection) compound risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Multiple realised revenue and cash-flow hits elevate severity to the upper-mid range.

evidence_list.snippet: We expect that cancellations or suspensions, reductions of services and failures to pay amounts due to us may increase at any time while the economic impact of the pandemic and the response to the pandemic impacts our customer base.

components.reason: Forecasts further deterioration in revenue and cash collections.
Timing open-ended (‘at any time’) adds uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking statement of possible worsening conditions yields a solid but not extreme score.

evidence_list.snippet: As a business, we have experienced and may continue to experience challenges, including increased costs, as we have and continue to pivot our employees’ work locations and hours as deemed necessary to respond to COVID-19 to protect the health and well-being of our employees, customers and community.

components.reason: Acknowledges incurred operational challenges and cost increases.
Highlights remote-work transition affecting labour arrangements.
Protective framing (‘to protect …’) indicates some mitigation effort.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational/labour impacts are present but partly offset by proactive mitigation, giving a mid-low score.

evidence_list.snippet: Any actual or perceived failure to comply with government orders, rules, laws or regulations as a result of changes in our operations in response to COVID-19 could subject us to investigations, claims, fines and other penalties, which in turn could adversely affect our business.

components.reason: Introduces additional regulatory/legal exposure linked to pandemic response.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Regulatory penalty risk is clear but hypothetical, justifying a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19, and the disruption in global economic conditions stemming from the pandemic, could also precipitate or aggravate the other risk factors discussed in this Report, which could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Notes cascading effect amplifying all other risk factors.
Uses strong ‘materially adversely’ language.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Systemic amplification of risks scores in the upper-mid range.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, the COVID-19 pandemic may also affect our operating and financial results in a manner that is not presently known to us or that we currently do not consider to present significant risks.

components.reason: Acknowledges unknown future impacts (unknown-unknowns).
Downplays significance (‘do not consider to present significant risks’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Unspecified risk tempered by qualifying language yields a very low score.

evidence_list.snippet: The real estate market may be adversely impacted by many different factors, including ... slowing transaction volumes due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic or otherwise that negatively impact investment returns;

components.reason: Connects COVID-19 to core industry demand (slower transactions).
Embedded within a broader list, diluting specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Industry-level linkage is acknowledged but generic; score remains modest.

evidence_list.snippet: Current general economic conditions in the U.S. and the world as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic are negatively affecting business operations for our clients and are expected to result in business consolidations and, in certain circumstances, failures.

components.reason: Identifies ongoing adverse effect on client base.
Forecasts consolidations and failures amplifying indirect risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Present client distress plus expected future consolidations drive a high but sub-maximum score.

evidence_list.snippet: We experienced a decrease in net new bookings of subscription-based services and an increase in customer requests for cancellations and suspensions towards the end of the first quarter of 2020 that continued through May 2020; however, those requests have eased since then, and sales related to marketplace service offerings have returned to pre-pandemic levels.

components.reason: Details realised downturn in bookings and spike in cancellations.
Highlights subsequent recovery, indicating mitigation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recovery offsets much of the initial impact, producing a minimal net risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic did not materially affect our consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2020.

components.reason: Affirmatively states no material 2020 financial impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear mitigation nullifies risk for this time frame, resulting in a zero score.

evidence_list.snippet: Overall, the increased direct spend related to the COVID-19 pandemic, including office reconfiguration, has not been material to date and has had minimal impact on our financial position and operating results as these expenses have been generally offset by the cost savings described above.

components.reason: Explicitly frames costs as immaterial and offset.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Statement is purely mitigating; under a recent-event context the net risk contribution is zero.
